name: Cessna 310R

climb.conditions: 2500 RPM and 24.5 inches Hg, landing gear up, wing flaps up, cowl flaps as required, 120 KIAS, mixtures at the recommended fuel flow. The handbook footnotes this figure "above 5200 feet, use full throttle": below that height the engines are throttled to hold 24.5 inches, so power stays put while drag falls with the air, and the rate of climb RISES with altitude up to about 5000 ft before falling away
climb.source: Pilot's Operating Handbook, Cessna Aircraft Company, 1976 Model 310R · P/N D1528-4-13 · Figure 5-15 · Rate-of-Climb - Cruise Climb

landing.conditions: Throttles idle, landing gear down, wing flaps 35 deg, cowl flaps closed, level hard surface runway, maximum braking effort
landing.source: Pilot's Operating Handbook, Cessna Aircraft Company, 1976 Model 310R · P/N D1528-4-13 · Figure 5-26 (Sheet 2 of 2) · Normal Landing Distance

stall.conditions: Throttles idle, 5500 lb gross weight. Gear up at flaps 0 deg; gear down at flaps 15 deg and 35 deg
stall.source: Pilot's Operating Handbook, Cessna Aircraft Company, 1976 Model 310R · P/N D1528-4-13 · Figure 5-8 · Stall Speeds

takeoff.conditions: Full throttle and 2700 RPM before brake release, mixtures leaned for field elevation, wing flaps up, cowl flaps open, level hard surface dry runway
takeoff.source: Pilot's Operating Handbook, Cessna Aircraft Company, 1976 Model 310R · P/N D1528-4-13 · Figure 5-10 (Sheet 2 of 2) · Normal Takeoff Distance
